hook: SCP-2828 is a part of your own body, sitting behind your ear, that you have never noticed and cannot notice without strong mnestics. Its rule is odd and precise: whichever sense you first perceive it with is the only sense that will ever work on it. Pay attention to how the file talks about describing the thing, because in this article the descriptions are part of the danger.
whyItMatters:
This is an Antimemetics Division file, and it shows how that kind of story can be built from a single rule about perception and language. The anomaly itself is harmless and practically inert; what is hazardous is knowing too much about it in the wrong order.

That makes the document self-aware in a useful way. Its procedures are mostly about controlling who reads which description, so the redactions feel like containment rather than decoration.
thingsToNotice:
The tests escalate cleanly. A D-class who first sees the structure can watch her own hand touch it and feel nothing, and in the next test a man blind from birth feels it and describes it, while the sighted subject cannot hear his words or read his typed note, which looks to her like moving letters and then a blank page.

Dr. J, who had heard both descriptions without ever perceiving the thing, asks for his own mnestics, and the test ends with the single line that he could not be saved; the later section explains that learning several sensory descriptions first means seizures, strokes and brain hemorrhage. The classified part then gives the reason this organ exists: it looks like a tiny ear, its frozen cells cannot be destroyed, and it guarded a spot on the throat against a nocturnal, highly intelligent species with innate mnestic ability that kept libraries on human anatomy and herded early humans like livestock. That predator died out, which leaves the organ with no remaining purpose except as a trap for Foundation staff, now tracked in personnel files listing which senses each person has been told about.
